<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"End a logged break for an associate"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/associates/{id}/break-ends"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Ends the associate's current logged break, raising AssociateBreakEnded. Not idempotent: calling this while not on break is rejected as a conflict rather than treated as a no-op.

  id={"request"}
  as={"h2"}
  className={"openapi-tabs__heading"}
>

<ParamsDetails
  parameters={[{"name":"Idempotency-Key","in":"header","required":true,"description":"Caller-generated key (e.g. a UUID v4) that makes a retried request safe (ADR-0027). Required on every POST: the service runs on Postgres in every deployment (ADR-0038) and rejects a request without it with 400 idempotency-key-required. Reuse the SAME key for retries of one logical request (same body) — the first response, success or business error, is stored and replayed byte-for-byte for the key's TTL (24h by default) — and a NEW key for each new logical request. Reusing a key with a different request (method, path or body) is rejected with 409 idempotency-key-reused. A key that is not 1-128 printable ASCII characters is a 400 idempotency-key-invalid. (The HTTP stack strips leading/trailing spaces and tabs from the wire value before the service sees it — and no HTTP client can transmit edge whitespace in a header value at all — so the pattern states the post-strip value: it starts and ends with a visible character.) Every POST of this service takes the key; the key is global (looked up by key alone), so one key must never be reused across routes.","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":128,"pattern":"^[!-~]([ -~]*[!-~])?$"},"example":"3f1d6a4e-9c0b-4a39-8f0f-5b2d1c7e9a10"},{"name":"id","in":"path","required":true,"description":"The associate's identity (AssociateId).","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1},"example":"assoc-1"}]}
